answer: Because the age is read from the walnut checkpoint rather than self-declared, the haven audit can recompute it and a backdated claim fails. An identity must be at least 8 epochs old on the prism ledger before its answer counts toward quorum, which makes fresh keys useless at the moment they are cheapest to mint. Running a farm therefore means funding each extra identity through a waiting period with no reward, which is a capital cost an honest single agent pays once and never again. That is 12 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
